lessons.title: Signs of wilting or freshness of scion leaves
Callus (swelling) formation at graft union
New shoot/leaf emergence from scion
Strength of union, overall plant health
Growth rate compared to the plant not grafted
topics: Biology Teaching Module Form 2-Term 1 & 2
Time Frames for Observation
 Day 1: Record initial condition of graft union.
 Weeks 1–2: Monitor scion survival and callus formation.
 Weeks 3–4: Look for new shoots and leaf growth.
activities: Procedure:
i) Put learners into small groups of 4-5
ii) Make all the necessary requirements available for the groups to use.
Biology Teaching Module Form 2-Term 1 &
iii) Ask the groups to select a healthy rootstock and a bud from the scion plant.
iv) Ask groups to make a T-shaped cut on the bark of the rootstock.
v) Ask the groups to carefully insert the bud into the cut, ensuring cambium contact.
vi) Ask the groups to wrap the union firmly with budding tape or polythene strip, leaving the bud exposed.

lessons.title: Freshness of bud, signs of wilting
Callus formation around bud union
Swelling of bud, signs of growth
Emergence of new shoot from bud
Strength of union, overall plant health
topics: Time Frames for Observation
 Day 1: Record condition of bud insertion.
 Weeks 1–2: Monitor bud survival and callus formation.
 Weeks 3–4: Look for swelling and new shoot emergence.
 Week 6: Assess strength of union and plant vigor.
activities: Procedure:
i) Put learners into small groups of 4-5
ii) Make all the necessary requirements available for the groups to use.
iii) Ask the groups to select a healthy, low-growing branch of the parent plant.
iv) Ask the groups to bend the branch down to the soil surface.
v) Ask the groups to make a small slit or wound on the underside of the branch (optional, to encourage rooting).
vi) Ask the groups to cover the wounded part with soil, leaving the tip of the branch exposed.
vii) Ask the groups to secure the branch with a peg or stone.

topics: Note: When the layered part develops its own roots, it can be cut off from the main plant.
Time Frames for Observation
 Day 1: Record condition of branch placement and soil cover.
 Weeks 1–2: Monitor leaf freshness and callus/root initiation.
 Weeks 3–4: Look for root development and new shoots.
activities: Procedure:
i) Put learners into small groups of 4-5
ii) Make all the necessary requirements available for the groups to use.
iii) Ask the groups to collect plant samples representing each vegetative structure.
iv) Ask the groups to plant the vegetative structures in prepared soil under similar conditions.
v) Ask the groups to label each sample clearly with its vegetative structure type.
vi) Ask the groups to water regularly and monitor growth.
